subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: On normal gateway SIGTERM/SIGINT, should OpenClaw cancel managed active/background exec child processes before the shutdown watchdog, preserve yielded/background work, or defer this behavior to a separate session/process control surface?
rationale: Current tests intentionally preserve active runs on normal shutdown, while the reported dirty shutdown requires changing that lifecycle contract or adding a bounded exception path.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Make normal stop reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting any explicit preservation exceptions.

options.title: Preserve background exec on normal stop
options.body: Keep the current contract and treat shutdown timeouts as expected when user work is still active, with better diagnostics for the responsible child process.

options.title: Defer to session kill/control design
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the broader sessions_kill or process ownership design so operators can list and terminate child work explicitly.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Make normal stop reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting any explicit preservation exceptions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history points to recent work across the gateway shutdown test and process-supervisor surfaces that need the policy decision.
